A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mouse–RL comparison and proposed methods. All 19 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL and LLM experiments and analyses of mouse trajectories, including behavioral statistics, replay experiments and appendix policy-divergence results.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental outcomes, including visitation overlap, waiting rates, replay experiments and policy-divergence analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed replay-rebalancing and amplification components and variance-penalized TD target remain. Renaming the replay components and clarifying their implementation do not establish a new algorithm; revised descriptions of experimental component use are addressed under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Cellworld predator-avoidance task, eight-mouse population, simulated environment, mouse-trajectory data and LLM scenario. No additional dataset, population or task condition is evaluated.

E2.justification: The online comparators and offline BC, CQL, COMBO and IQL comparisons remain represented. Appendix E revises baseline equations and replaces inconsistent SAC/TDMPC-2 naming with generic 'online RL' terminology, without demonstrating that a different comparator was evaluated.

E3.justification: v1 explicitly describes Figure 8 as using 50% selective-memory sampling. v3 describes standard versus amplified TDMPC-2 and states that long-term TISB experiments primarily used amplification. This revises the reported component configuration without establishing reruns. Training budgets, timestep, sample counts and checkpoint-selection procedures otherwise remain.

E4.justification: v1 Figure 17 shows how BC, COMBO, CQL and IQL rewards and episode lengths evolve with training; v3 removes this training-dynamics evidence. The replay-ratio sensitivity study, amplification comparison, trajectory examples, episode-length distributions and KL analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five random seeds for Figure 7, standard-deviation shading for movement analyses, and standard deviations in Figure 13. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation procedures or significance tests are added or changed.

E6.justification: v3 removes the offline training curves, PER's reported reward improvement of about 5 after 50,000 steps, and the claim that mice spend over 50% of their time assessing the environment. Headline overlap values of 20.9% and 86.1%, waiting rates, and KL divergence of 6.4386 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix E substantively revises the CQL and COMBO mathematical objectives. IQL's previous max-based value equation is replaced with expectile regression and separate value/Q losses. These are localized mathematical revisions to baseline descriptions; the proposed TD target remains unchanged and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction weakens its precise claim that mice spend 'over 50%' of their time gathering information to 'a significant amount of time.' The abstract's central behavioral-gap claim and the two proposed mechanisms remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 8 adds an explanation linking risky RL behavior to the absence of irreversible mortality, with connections to imagination and planning. v3 also removes the explicit warning that replay rebalancing can become counterproductive later in training, while retaining broader instability, behavioral-fidelity and generality limitations.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly identifies negative rewards as the quantity amplified by 200, clarifies that 300 steps is the maximum episode length, and defines success rate. These improve implementation and evaluation documentation without establishing changed numerical hyperparameters.

R1.justification: Five references are added concerning curiosity-driven learning, mortal computation, imagination-augmented agents and the evolution of planning. They support limited extensions to Sections 7–8 rather than a broad repositioning of the contribution.

P1.justification: Section 5.1 renames the replay components, Appendix E receives expanded motivation and rewritten explanations, and the discussion gains a paragraph. Terminology and grammar are also edited, while the overall section and appendix structure remains.

P2.justification: Several plots receive revised axes, legends, color bars or captions. Figures 10 and 11 exchange order, and the offline training plot is removed. The retained KL plot becomes Figure 17 instead of Figure 18; these are localized display changes.

improvement.justification: v3 offers a limited net improvement in technical clarity through explicit reward-amplification details, clearer figure labeling and the revised offline-RL mathematics, especially IQL's expectile formulation. The gains are tempered by removal of the offline learning curves and the late-training replay caveat. The central empirical evidence and its limitations remain largely unchanged.
